sourceLabel: User-supplied ISAM table; claims have not been independently verified

sectors.title: Active debris removal and end-of-life services

programmes.description: Mission Extension Vehicle (MEV) docks to client satellites and takes over station-keeping. Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV) uses two robotic arms (DARPA/NRL RSGS payload) to install Mission Extension Pods (MEPs) as add-on propulsion.
programmes.status: MEV-1 serviced Intelsat 901 (2020–25) and Optus D3 (2025–Aug 2026); MEV-2 docked to Intelsat 10-02 in 2021. MRV and three MEPs launched 21 Jul 2026. Under Optus's Project Aurora, the MRV is to install an MEP on Optus D3 in late 2027 (up to six years' extension); SES is also a customer.

programmes.description: Passive and Active Refuelling Modules (PRM/ARM); GAS-T GEO tanker carrying up to 1000 kg of hydrazine.
programmes.status: PRM selected as USSF preferred refuelling interface (2024). USSF Elixir refuelling demonstration awarded Apr 2025; launch date undisclosed.

programmes.description: Otter servicer docks with satellites not designed for servicing, for life extension, inspection or disposal.
programmes.status: Otter Pup 1 (2023) completed RPO without docking; Otter Pup 2 (2025) is attempting to dock with Gilmour's ElaraSat. First full Otter launched 1 Oct 2026 for NASA SSPICY (inspections from 2027). Intelsat and USSF GEO missions and an SDA disposal mission (2027) under contract.

programmes.description: Robotic capture and reboost of spacecraft not designed for servicing. Acquired Atomos Space (2025).
programmes.status: LINK launched 3 Jul 2026 to reboost NASA's Swift. Two of three reaction wheels failed and the cold-gas RCS was degraded, causing a tumble. Reboost abandoned 19 Aug 2026 after RPO to 12–15 km; LINK re-entered 25 Sep 2026.

programmes.description: LEXI-P servicer docks with GEO satellites and provides attitude and orbit control for life extension.
programmes.status: In development after repeated slips; expected to be launch-ready in 2027.

programmes.description: APS-R refueller transfers hydrazine to USSF satellites in GEO and tops up at an Orbit Fab depot.
programmes.status: Launch slipped from mid-2026 to 2027 on a USSF mission. First client is an AFRL Tetra-5 satellite.

programmes.description: Close-range inspection of non-cooperative objects (ADRAS-J, ISSA-J1).
programmes.status: ADRAS-J approached an H-IIA upper stage to ≈15 m (Dec 2024), the closest commercial approach to large debris. ISSA-J1 to inspect two retired Japanese satellites (ALOS, ADEOS-II); launch 2027.

programmes.description: Removal of prepared satellites via magnetic docking plate (ELSA) and capture of unprepared rocket bodies (ADRAS-J2).
programmes.status: ELSA-d (2021) demonstrated magnetic capture. ADRAS-J2 launch FY2027; ELSA-M (OneWeb) slipped to FY2028 or later, both on Isar Spectrum. Lost UK national ADR contract to ClearSpace (Aug 2026).

programmes.description: Endurance vehicle (≈750 kg) docks with unprepared GEO satellites for ≈5 years of life extension. OrbitGuard smallsats provide GEO inspection.
programmes.status: OrbitGuard-1 in GEO since 2023. Endurance orders from Hispasat, SES (Nov 2025) and Eutelsat (Sep 2026); first launch planned 2027.

programmes.description: GEA servicer (ESA RISE mission) docks with GEO satellites and takes over attitude and orbit control for life extension, relocation or disposal.
programmes.status: EUR 119.6M ESA contract (Oct 2024), with Eutelsat as partner. Launch planned 2028.

programmes.description: D3 propulsive decommissioning device for controlled de-orbit, even of unresponsive satellites.
programmes.status: Demonstrated on D-SAT (2017).

programmes.description: EROSS IOD: robotic servicer with a Leonardo arm for capture, refuelling and payload exchange in LEO.
programmes.status: EUR 235M Italian Space Agency contract (2023). System preliminary design review completed (Oct 2025); launch date not announced.

programmes.description: ARCap autonomous rendezvous-and-capture module for non-cooperative targets (life extension, relocation, debris removal).
programmes.status: Seed-funded (US$4M); no flight yet. First ARCap flight was earlier targeted for 2025–26.

programmes.description: VEDA servicer with a docking and propellant-transfer interface for life extension, refuelling and de-orbit.
programmes.status: Raised ≈US$10.5M (Aug 2026) to fund four in-orbit demonstration missions over 12–18 months.

programmes.description: Electric-propulsion spacevan transfer vehicle, being extended to rendezvous, docking and in-orbit services (CNES study).
programmes.status: Spacevan-002 delivered NASA's AEPEX cubesat (May 2026). First GEO spacevan manifested on Ariane 64 (planned H2 2026); further CNES GEO mission planned 2028.

programmes.description: Modular Port platform to host, service and integrate payloads in orbit, with a Cutter vehicle for docking and transfer.
programmes.status: Commercial sustaining partner for NASA's Astrobee free-flying robots on the ISS (back in operation Jan 2026). Cutter first flight planned late 2026 to early 2027.

programmes.description: Robotic spacecraft (Orbots) for inspection (Laura) and relocation and servicing (Fred).
programmes.status: Barry-1 sensor and computing testbed flown (Nov 2023); AFRL research agreement. Laura-1 RPO demonstration (targeted 2025) not yet reported flown.

programmes.description: Hydrazine depots and tankers using the RAFTI refuelling port and GRIP nozzle.
programmes.status: Tanker-001 Tenzing (2021) and Podracer (hosted on Momentus Vigoride, Mar 2026) in LEO. RAFTI accepted by USSF. Kamino GEO depot (with Impulse Space) planned 2027.

programmes.organisation: China Academy of Space Technology (CAST, China)
programmes.description: Shijian-25 GEO refuelling and life-extension servicer. Shijian-21 had towed a dead BeiDou satellite to graveyard orbit (2022).
programmes.status: SJ-25 (launched Jan 2025) docked with SJ-21 in mid-2025; separation observed Nov 2025. Widely assessed as the first GEO satellite-to-satellite refuelling; not officially detailed.

programmes.description: Flexible continuum robotic arm for autonomous refuelling; drag-sphere de-orbit device.
programmes.status: Xiyuan-0 launched 16 Mar 2026; completed refuelling simulations with its arm and deployed a 2.5 m drag sphere.

programmes.description: Standardised docking and refuelling interface; tanker and target smallsats for LEO refuelling.
programmes.status: AayulSAT lost in the PSLV-C62 failure (12 Jan 2026). Two-satellite docking, refuelling and orbit-raising demonstration targeted Q1 2027.

programmes.description: Starship ship-to-ship cryogenic propellant transfer, required for the Artemis lunar lander (HLS).
programmes.status: Not yet flown; demonstration no earlier than late 2026.

programmes.description: LOXSAT liquid-oxygen fluid-management demonstrator (NASA Tipping Point), precursor to the Cryo-Dock depot (2030).
programmes.status: Integrated on a Rocket Lab Photon bus. Electron launch has slipped repeatedly since Jul 2026; not flown as of late Sep 2026.

programmes.description: Blue Ring mobility platform for hosting, transport and in-orbit refuelling from MEO to cislunar space.
programmes.status: Blue Ring Pathfinder flew attached to the New Glenn upper stage (Jan 2025). No free-flying Blue Ring mission yet.

programmes.description: Hydrogen-peroxide green propulsion aimed at in-orbit refuelling, life-extension and de-orbit services.
programmes.status: Green-propulsion system test-fired on PSLV-C60's POEM-4 platform (Dec 2024). Refuelling, life-extension and de-orbit services under development.

programmes.description: Non-Earth imaging of space objects using hosted cameras and repurposed Earth-observation satellites.
programmes.status: Commercial inspection service operating in LEO, including RPO around a CZ-2C rocket body. GEO capability targeted late 2026.

programmes.description: DROID spacecraft for space-domain awareness and inspection, evolving towards docking and de-orbit.
programmes.status: DROID.001 (2023) and DROID.002 (Mar 2025) flown; DROID.003 planned 2026.

programmes.description: Jackal autonomous vehicles for RPO and characterisation of non-cooperative objects.
programmes.status: Jackal pursued an evading Rocket Lab spacecraft in the USSF Victus Haze demonstration (Jun–Jul 2026).

programmes.description: Optimus servicing and inspection spacecraft; Optimus Viper for rapid-response inspection.
programmes.status: Optimus-1 (Mar 2024) lost contact after launch. 450 kg Optimus for the Space MAITRI debris-inspection mission on ISRO's SSLV, no earlier than Q4 2026.

programmes.description: LINUSS cubesats demonstrating near-GEO RPO for in-space upgrade and servicing.
programmes.status: Two 12U cubesats (launched Nov 2022) manoeuvred to within ≈200 m of each other (2023).

programmes.description: Owl optical sensors with onboard AI for characterising space objects and supporting RPO.
programmes.status: First Owl awaits launch on Blue Origin's first Blue Ring mission (planned spring 2026, not yet flown). US$18M Series A (May 2026).

programmes.description: Multi-arm robotic capture and de-orbit of unprepared objects; Phoenix GEO life-extension vehicle.
programmes.status: UK national ADR contract (GBP 61.3M, Aug 2026) to remove two UK satellites by the early 2030s. ESA ClearSpace-1 (target PROBA-1) ≈2028–29; PRELUDE RPO demonstration 2027; ESA Phoenix contract (Sep 2026).

programmes.description: Laelaps relocation and de-orbit spacecraft with the REACCH multi-arm grappling end-effector.
programmes.status: REACCH prototype completed 172 capture cycles on the ISS (Nov 2024–May 2025). First full spacecraft planned 2027.

programmes.description: Inflatable Capture Bag that envelops tumbling debris or small asteroids.
programmes.status: Capture Bag deployed and inflated on the ISS (Oct 2025).

programmes.description: Space-based pulsed-laser ablation to detumble and de-orbit debris (SKY Perfect JSAT spin-off).
programmes.status: Prototype planned 2027; services targeted from 2029.

programmes.description: Ground-based lasers to slow and de-orbit small (<10 cm) debris.
programmes.status: Seed-funded; ground development.

programmes.description: Small-body and debris capture technologies for resource and debris missions.
programmes.status: NEO-01 microsatellite (Apr 2021) launched to trial net-based debris capture.

programmes.description: DRUMS microsatellite demonstrating approach to and capture of debris.
programmes.status: DRUMS (launched Nov 2021) released mock debris and demonstrated approach and simulated capture (Dec 2023).

programmes.description: Laser tracking of debris; high-power laser to de-orbit satellites by ablation or photon pressure.
programmes.status: Operates laser debris-tracking stations. High-power laser de-orbit demonstration expected ≈2027 (announced Sep 2025).

programmes.description: ADEO deployable drag sails (1.7–25 m2) for passive de-orbit.
programmes.status: ADEO sail deployed in orbit from D-Orbit's ION carrier (Dec 2022). 25 m2 ADEO-L integrated on the Redwire-built EU demonstration satellite Σyndeo-3, launch planned 2026.

programmes.description: Spinnaker drag sails to de-orbit satellites and upper stages of up to 1000 kg.
programmes.status: Acquired by Applied Aerospace & Defense (Feb 2026).

programmes.description: HORN mechanically deployed drag sail for post-mission disposal.
programmes.status: First in-orbit demonstration on H3 Flight 6 succeeded (Jun 2026).

programmes.description: SWEEPER spacecraft using computer vision and AI to capture and de-orbit debris.
programmes.status: Concept stage; first mission planned to de-orbit 40 objects (announced 2024), not yet flown.

programmes.description: Space robotics with Canadarm heritage; SKYMAKER commercial robotics for servicing and assembly.
programmes.status: Canadarm3 (C$1.0B contract, no earlier than 2029) continues, but its use is uncertain after NASA paused Gateway (2026).

programmes.description: Autonomous robotic arms and robotic servicing satellites (RPO, docking, life extension, de-orbit).
programmes.status: S2 arm demonstrated outside the ISS (Mar 2024). S3 servicing-satellite flight model completed (Jun 2026); launch deferred beyond 2028 to prioritise USSF interceptor work.

programmes.description: iSSI androgynous mechanical, power and data interface for modular, serviceable spacecraft.
programmes.status: Flight-proven on the ISS (TRL 7). SpaceDREAM arm-and-interface demonstration with KINETIK Space awaits RFA One's maiden flight.

programmes.description: Off-the-shelf rendezvous, proximity operations and docking (RPOD) kit.
programmes.status: RPO software tested in orbit for 17 months. CSA funding (C$1M, 2025–27) to mature hardware for a first flight.

programmes.description: xLink modular robotic arms; ModuLink robotics kit (with Blue Origin) for servicing and reconfiguring spacecraft.
programmes.status: DIU ModuLink contract with Blue Origin (2022). xLink's planned flight on OSAM-2 lapsed when NASA ended that mission (2023).

programmes.description: TITAN 7-DoF robotic arm for on-orbit servicing and debris removal.
programmes.status: ESA-funded prototype (contract >EUR 2.5M, 2020) completed environmental testing (2025); ready for integration into servicing missions.

programmes.description: SIROM standard interface combining mechanical, electrical, data and thermal connections.
programmes.status: 13 units built and ground-validated in EU and ESA projects; preparing an in-orbit demonstration.

programmes.description: HOTDOCK standard interface (mechanical, data, power, fluid) for robotic servicing and assembly.
programmes.status: Used in several EU and ESA ground demonstrations; no flight reported.

programmes.description: DogTag universal grapple fixtures that make satellites easier to capture for servicing or removal.
programmes.status: More than 300 DogTags flown on OneWeb satellites (by Feb 2022).

programmes.description: SPIDER robotic arm to assemble a 3 m antenna on NASA's OSAM-1.
programmes.status: OSAM-1 cancelled by NASA (Mar 2024). Lanteris acquired by Intuitive Machines (Jan 2026).

programmes.description: TESSERAE electromagnetic tiles that self-assemble into large structures.
programmes.status: Two ISS demonstrations completed; third ISS test in 2026. First free-flying autonomous assembly mission planned late 2026 or early 2027.

programmes.description: Electron-beam welding, cutting and robotic assembly of large platforms (ThinkPlatform); also proposes harvesting aluminium debris for recycling into fuel.
programmes.status: Autonomous e-beam welds made on a recoverable Falcon 9-hosted payload (May 2024) and returned; second flight Dec 2024. ThinkPlatform-1 ≈2027–28.

programmes.description: Robotic in-space 3D printing and assembly of large (up to km-scale) RF antennas.
programmes.status: USSF SBIR and other contracts (>US$3M); ground development with Axiom Space, Northrop Grumman and SwRI.

programmes.description: Robotic in-orbit assembly of the km-scale CASSIOPeiA space-based solar power satellite.
programmes.status: AlbaTRUSS ground demonstration of robotic truss assembly with UKAEA (2025). In-orbit demonstrator planned 2028; power from space targeted for ≈2030.

programmes.organisation: Above: Space Development (USA; formerly Orbital Assembly)
programmes.description: Automated truss-building machine (DSTAR) for robotically assembled rotating stations.
programmes.status: Full-scale DSTAR prototype demonstrated on the ground. Station projects unfunded; no flight hardware.

programmes.description: Free-flying W-series capsules for microgravity pharmaceutical processing, also used as hypersonic re-entry testbeds.
programmes.status: Six missions flown (2023–26), five capsules recovered (W-4 failed re-entry). W-8 and W-9 launched 1 Oct 2026.

programmes.description: ForgeStar free-flyers for semiconductor crystal growth; Pridwen deployable heat shield for return.
programmes.status: ForgeStar-1 (Jun 2025) reached 1000 °C and generated plasma in its furnace (Dec 2025). ForgeStar-2, the first material-return attempt, planned 2026–27.

programmes.description: ISS facilities for pharmaceutical crystallisation (PIL-BOX) and bioprinting (BFF); formerly Made In Space (Archinaut).
programmes.status: Repeated PIL-BOX flights (Eli Lilly, BMS); bioprinted cardiac tissue (2024). Archinaut One (OSAM-2) ended by NASA before flight (2023).

programmes.description: ESA metal 3D printer (wire-fed, laser) on the ISS.
programmes.status: First metal parts printed in orbit (2024). Samples returned for analysis 2025–26; fifth print retrieved 2026.

programmes.description: Drawing ZBLAN fluoride-glass optical fibre in microgravity on the ISS.
programmes.status: ≈12 km of fibre drawn (2024). Space-drawn fibre showed lower attenuation (peer-reviewed, 2026).

programmes.description: Layer-by-layer manufacture of protein-based artificial retinas in microgravity.
programmes.status: Nine ISS investigations. First free-flyer mission (Helogen platform on a D-Orbit vehicle) scheduled for Oct 2026.

programmes.description: Automated CubeLab and Mambo facilities for microgravity R&D and manufacturing on the ISS.
programmes.status: Mambo facility delivered to the ISS (Aug 2024).

programmes.description: Microgravity crystal-growth furnace for high-purity silicon semiconductors.
programmes.status: NASA parabolic-flight tests. Free-flyer demonstration with SpaceWorks (NASA TechLeap) planned 2027.

programmes.description: Heat-free photopolymer 3D printing of structures in vacuum, e.g. solar-array supports.
programmes.status: Replicator flew on the Ariane 6 maiden flight (Jul 2024). Replicator-2 launched 7 Jul 2026.

companies.name: ATMOS Space Cargo (Germany) and Space Cargo Unlimited

programmes.organisation: ATMOS Space Cargo (Germany) and Space Cargo Unlimited (France)
programmes.description: Phoenix re-entry capsules with inflatable heat shield, carrying the BentoBox platform for microgravity production and return.
programmes.status: Phoenix 1 (Apr 2025) met primary objectives but was not recovered. Phoenix 2, first of seven BentoBox missions, scheduled for H2 2026.

programmes.description: ELS-R small re-entry satellites for microgravity experiments and manufacturing with sample return.
programmes.status: First satellite (AOBA) booked on Isar Spectrum for H2 2026; not yet launched.

programmes.description: Dream Chaser spaceplane for low-g return of space-made products; manufacturing agreements with Astral Materials and Space Forge.
programmes.status: Agreements signed Dec 2024. Dream Chaser first flight, now a free-flyer demonstration without ISS docking, slipped to late 2026.

programmes.description: HEL-IOS autonomous orbital biomanufacturing system for biomaterials and proteins.
programmes.status: Two missions scheduled for Oct 2026, one carrying LambdaVision's retina proteins on a D-Orbit vehicle.

programmes.description: AMP-1 microfabrication platform that prints nerve-repair implants and tissue in microgravity.
programmes.status: AMP-1 on the ISS since Nov 2024; printed eight nerve implants (2025). AXLM-3 mission (returned Jun 2026) produced kidney, liver and cartilage tissue and 28 implants.

programmes.description: Orbital High-Throughput Screener for automated drug screening (>2000 samples per mission).
programmes.status: ISS mission contracted with Voyager (May 2026); agreement to fly on Outpost's Carryall return vehicle (Oct 2026).

programmes.description: Microgravity crystallisation of monoclonal antibodies for high-concentration injectable formulations.
programmes.status: Re-entry survivability test on The Exploration Company's capsule (2025). Baby BOX-E, the largest drug-crystallisation run in space to date, launched to the ISS (May 2026).

programmes.description: Bulk crystal growth of semiconductor and semimetal alloys in microgravity.
programmes.status: ISS experiment in NASA's SUBSA furnace (launched Nov 2024). Payload reservation on Starlab for commercial-scale production (Mar 2026).

programmes.description: Microgravity lab and contract-research services (Lab-as-a-Service, ScienceTaxi) for biotech.
programmes.status: More than 25 ISS research missions. ScienceTaxi BioForge bioprinter passed ESA critical design review (Jun 2026); first flight planned 2027.

programmes.description: Recover aluminium from old upper stages for in-space and lunar construction (ALReCo aluminium–regolith composite).
programmes.status: Concept stage: ESA OSIP business-case study (2021) and ground prototypes. No flight mission announced.

programmes.description: Melt captured debris into metal rods that Neumann's solid-metal electric thruster uses as propellant (CisLunar Modular Space Foundry).
programmes.status: SpaceWERX Orbital Prime concept (US$1.7M, 2023) with Astroscale U.S. and Colorado State University. Neumann Drive flight-tested on several smallsats (2024–26).

programmes.description: Triton payload captures 20–50 small (<1 m) debris pieces per mission; designed to deliver them to future recycling stations.
programmes.status: Ground demonstration (May 2025); not yet flown. Partnered with Portal Space Systems (Mar 2026) for a debris-removal service from 2027; ISS demonstration planned late 2026 or early 2027. Full capture units are currently ejected to burn up on re-entry rather than recycled.

programmes.description: Solid-metal plasma thrusters that can use a wide range of metals, including recovered debris, as propellant.
programmes.status: Rogue demonstration (launched Jun 2025, ended Feb 2026) verified charging and plasma generation but performed no manoeuvres. Warlock (2027) and Paladin (>1 N, 2028) thrusters planned.

programmes.description: Outpost concept: robotic cutting and repurposing of spent upper stages into platforms and habitats.
programmes.status: Outpost Mars Demo-1 (May 2022) cut corrosion-resistant steel in orbit by friction milling without creating debris. No follow-on flight reported.

programmes.organisation: DEXTER consortium (Cranfield Univ., SENER, Magdrive, Univ. Alicante, Moliri, Vimotek)
programmes.description: Robotic harvesting tools, vacuum laser cutting and conversion of scrap aluminium into thruster propellant.
programmes.status: EU-funded (EUR 4.0M, Oct 2025–Sep 2029); laboratory demonstrations under way.

programmes.description: Captures small debris and sorts it as feedstock for in-space additive manufacturing.
programmes.status: Early-stage concept; no flight hardware announced.

programmes.description: Refabricator recycles plastic waste into 3D-printer filament; also KRAKEN robotic arm.
programmes.status: Refabricator, the first integrated recycler and 3D printer in space, completed at least seven recycle-and-print cycles on the ISS (2019).

programmes.description: Concept for an orbital station that repairs, repurposes and recycles defunct satellites.
programmes.status: Concept studies only (published 2019); operation envisaged by 2050.
